newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians hunt for lucrative cockroaches.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians hunt for lucrative cockroaches.

text.p: Brazilians are catching cockroaches with their barehands, all in the name of science and a bit of extra cash, local Globo television said on Sunday.
Strong-stomached residents of Rio have been selling batches of roaches to a laboratory for $25 per 3.35 ounces (100 grams) of the insects, Globo said.
"You give them a quick slap and then grab them by their antennae, it's not a big deal," said housewife Elvira Martinez de Oliveira as she proudly showed off her still wriggling prey.

The laboratory, which placed a "We buy cockroaches" advertisement in a local newspaper, is researching a possible vaccine to a series of allergies. The vaccine is based on substances found in the pests.
"Two or three percent of substances that cause allergies come from cockroaches shedding their skin," said researcher Gilberto Pradez.
To complete its research, the laboratory needs 11 pounds (five kg) of the insects, equivalent to 600,000 cockroaches, Globo said.
